svg.aria-label: How to open a conversation with someone you are worried about, without exposing her. First, choose a place where she is genuinely alone, not within earshot of the group and not in front of her children. Second, choose a moment that has an innocent explanation, such as walking somewhere together or helping with a task. Third, do not use a message, because a phone may be shared, checked or monitored; call instead and let her control the timing. Then say: I have noticed you seem worried lately. Is there anything you would like support with? Then stop talking, because the silence is the part that works. The question names what you have seen without accusing anyone, and it can be answered with no at no cost to her. If she says no, accept it warmly, say the offer stands, and behave normally afterwards.
svg.text: Before you say anything
The whole risk lives in where, when and how.
Somewhere alone
Not within earshot of the group.
Not in a doorway. Not in front of
her children, who may be asked
later what was said.
A moment that looks ordinary
Walking somewhere together.
Helping with a task. A reason to
be talking that anyone watching
would find unremarkable.
Never by message
A phone may be shared, checked
or already monitored. If you must
use one, call rather than write and
let her control the timing.
THEN SAY
“I have noticed you seem worried lately.
Is there anything you would like support with?”
Then stop talking. The silence is the part that works.
It names what you have seen without accusing anyone, and it offers rather than asks.
She can answer “no, I am fine” at no cost, which is what makes it safe for her to say yes.
Treasured Vessels Girls’ Centre · treasuredvesselsuganda.org
